assertions.text: Output contains at least one markdown table
Table covers cancellation rules — includes rows for states where cancellation is allowed and where it is not
The 30-day return window rule is addressed — either as a threshold column, a separate table, or flagged as an open question
Uses value sets {PENDING, CONFIRMED} or equivalent to express 'regardless of which starting state' for cases where a rule holds across states
At least one output column ends with '?'
Table has a scenario/description column as the leftmost column
Each row is independently verifiable — no row references a prior row's outcome. Each row specifies its own starting state and expected result.

Multiple tables (or @TableTest methods) are used, each addressing a distinct concern — not one monolithic table mixing unrelated rules. Acceptable to use a single table only when the domain genuinely has a single concern.
Each table has only the rows needed to express its concern's rules — no unnecessary permutations from combining concerns. Fewer rows per table is expected when concerns are properly separated.
Status transition rules and return eligibility rules are in separate tables
